chunks: Ahmad narrated from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah, from Aban, from Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him: Where does the Mutamatti' (one performing Hajj al-Tamattu') cease the Talbiyah? He said: 'When he enters the houses, the houses of Mecca, not the houses of al-Abtah.'

key_terms.التَّلْبِيَةِ: The ritual proclamation of 'Labbayk' recited during Hajj
key_terms.الْأَبْطَحِ: Al-Abtah, a specific area outside the main city boundary near the Haram
key_terms.الْمُتَمَتِّعُ: The pilgrim who performs Hajj al-Tamattu' (combining Umrah and Hajj)
key_terms.بُيُوتَ مَكَّةَ: The houses of Mecca (the city proper)

ai.seo_question: When does a pilgrim stop reciting Talbiyah during Hajj al-Tamattu'?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the specific boundary for terminating the Talbiyah for Mu'tamirun, distinguishing between the general urban area of Mecca and the specific precinct of al-Abtah. This distinction is significant in Shia jurisprudence for determining the exact moment the pilgrim transitions from the state of Ihram's ritual declarations to the preparation for Tawaf, ensuring the ritual is performed with precise adherence to the Imam's guidance.
